## 1.8 million SEK for research on infections and heart attacks
*Fri, 13 Nov 2026 12:45:40 +0100*

Why do some people suffer a heart attack in connection with an infection? With 1.8 million SEK in funding from the Swedish Heart-Lung Foundation, researchers at Umeå University will investigate which infections carry the highest risk and which individuals are particularly vulnerable.

[Read more](https://www.umu.se/nyheter/18-miljoner-till-forskning-om-infektioner-och-hjartinfarkt_4275162/)

## Umeå University strengthens ties with Newcastle University through EC2U
*Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:51:55 +0100*

When Newcastle University joins the EC2U Alliance as a full partner in 2027, new opportunities will open up for collaboration in education, research and mobility. For Umeå University, it will provide an opportunity to deepen ties with a university with which it already has several established connections.

[Read more](https://www.umu.se/nyheter/umea-university-fordjupar-samarbetet-med-newcastle-university-ec2u_4275023/)

## New approach balances growth and seasonal responses in aspen
*Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:40:02 +0100*

Increasing tree growth without disrupting the trees' seasonal rhythm is a challenge. Researchers at Umeå Plant Science Centre have now developed an approach that allows aspen trees to grow more while still responding to the changing seasons. The key lies in a connection between the trees’ internal clock and the production of a growth-promoting hormone.

[Read more](https://www.umu.se/nyheter/ny-metod-okar-aspens-tillvaxt-utan-att-stora-arstidsrytmen_4274972/)

*Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:20:03 +0100*

Uncovering overlooked aspects of Sámi history, disrupting bacteria’s hiding places and using AI to detect aggressive prostate cancer are just some of the aims of 21 EU-funded projects involving researchers at Umeå University.

## Physicists receive ERC Synergy Grant to create extreme light pulses
*Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:20:47 +0100*

With the “ExtremeField” project, researchers aim to push the boundaries of physics by focusing laser light in a new way. Their goal is to create light pulses that have so far been impossible to achieve, reaching intensities a million times beyond the current state of the art. The project is funded by an ERC Synergy Grant totaling almost SEK 150 million, of which SEK 60 million will go to Umeå University.

[Read more](https://www.umu.se/nyheter/fysiker-far-erc-synergy-grant-for-att-skapa-extrema-ljuspulser_4274504/)

## Strong interest in Northern Star Fellows: "A real success"
*Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:56:53 +0100*

More than 2,000 applications have been submitted for the assistant professor positions in the new Umeå University Northern Star Fellows excellence programme. The applications have come from many parts of the world. 
"It has been a real success," says Tora Holmberg, Vice-Chancellor of Umeå University.

## Laura Bacete Cano reflects on the STS Forum in Kyoto
*Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:52:57 +0100*

Researchers, policymakers and industry leaders from around the world gathered in Kyoto in October for the Science and Technology in Society Forum (STS Forum). Laura Bacete Cano, researcher at Umeå Plant Science Centre and member of the Young Academy of Sweden, took part in both the forum and its Young Leaders Program. One of her main takeaways was that taking part in discussions about the future of science is part of the job as a researcher, not something separate from it.

[Read more](https://www.umu.se/nyheter/laura-bacete-cano-reflekterar-over-sts-forum-i-kyoto_4273424/)

## Recreating heatwaves in the lab to help older people stay well at home
*Thu, 05 Nov 2026 12:00:11 +0100*

A climate chamber, virtual environments and technology that monitors the body and brain. Using these resources, researchers at Umeå University will identify ways to protect older adults’ mental well-being during heatwaves at home.

[Read more](https://www.umu.se/nyheter/varmeboljor-aterskapas-i-labbet-for-att-hjalpa-aldre-att-ma-bra_4273115/)
